name: COUPDAYBS
description: COUPDAYBS returns the number of days between the start of the current coupon period and the settlement date for a bond.
tldr: Calculates the number of days from the beginning of the coupon period to the settlement date.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.description: Days from coupon start to settlement
basicExample.explanation: For a bond purchased on April 1, 2024 with semi-annual coupons, this returns the number of days since the coupon period began.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/actual basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 counts actual days in the actual year.

howItWorks: COUPDAYBS is used in bond pricing to determine accrued interest. It identifies where the settlement date falls within the current coupon period.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Settlement date must be before maturity date.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: COUPDAYBS works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between COUPDAYBS and COUPDAYS?
faq.answer: COUPDAYBS counts days from the coupon start to settlement. COUPDAYS counts days in the entire coupon period.

faq.question: Why is COUPDAYBS used?
faq.answer: It is used to calculate accrued interest for bond trades.
